newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - ROFF TAKES OVER FROM THE GREAT ENTERTAINER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - ROFF TAKES OVER FROM THE GREAT ENTERTAINER.

text.p: Joe Roff replaces the greatest entertainer of the age at Edinburgh's Murrayfield on Saturday where Australia take on Scotland in the first international of their tour of Britain and Ireland.
Sentiment plays little part in Australian sport and the selectors have decided to omit 34-year-old David Campese, the world record try scorer, and play 21-year-old Roff on the right wing.

Campese may yet take the field in the first international to be played under the new rules allowing tactical substitutions but clearly the Wallabies are now looking to the future and the 1999 World Cup in Wales.
"This Australian side is in the transitional stage but we have some wonderful backs, even though the selection decision was taken to leave leave out David Campese," said captain John Eales.
"Tim Horan and Joe Roff are brilliant finishers, while Pat Howard and Danny Herbert have been around for a long time."
Centre Howard echoed Eales's observations, commenting: "We are going through a transition period and building towards the next World Cup, so there is a huge amount of competition for a place."
Eales himself is a model of the new rugby union professional, a lock with the speed of a loose forward who can kick goals for good measure.

He leads a team who finished a clear third behind New Zealand and South Africa in the first Tri-Nations series this year and who have also been affected by injuries and appalling weather on the Scotland leg of their tour.
The Wallabies have also not been helped by remarks from Queensland coach John Connolly who has claimed there is a rift in the camp.
"There are a few people trying to destabilise the Wallaby camp," said coach Greg Smith.
"Generally, Australians are very supportive of the team but there are a few with access to the media who are not."
Scotland supplied some of the best rugby of a admittedly drab Five Nations' season this year due mainly to the enterprise and invention of Gregor Townsend at fly-half.
Townsend, who will captain the side in the absence of the injured Rob Wainwright, has moved into the centres to allow Craig Chalmers resume his partnership with scrum-half Gary Armstrong.
"Gregor Townsend can be dynamite wherever he plays in midfield for Scotland," Eales added.
"And we know that their half-backs, Craig Chalmers and Gary Armstrong, have the experience and skill to influence and win a tight test match."
Townsend added: "We played some excellent rugby in the first three games of the Five Nations' championship but could not carry it through to the end.

"We want to return to that sort of enterprising rugby, while building on the lessons we learned during our defeats in New Zealand in the summer. The only way to play is to use all 15 players and exploit the freedom they get under the new laws."
Teams:

Scotland - Rowen Shepherd; Tony Stanger, Gregor Townsend (captain), Ron Eriksson, Kenny Logan; Craig Chalmers, Gary Armstrong; Eric Peters, Ian Smith, Murray Wallace, Damian Cronin, Doddie Weir, David Hilton, Kevin McKenzie, Barry Stewart.

Australia - Matthew Burke; Tim Horan, Daniel Herbert, Pat Howard, Joe Roff; David Knox, Sam Payne; Daniel Manu, David Wilson, Owen Finegan, John Eales (captain), Warwick Waugh, Andrew Blades, Michael Foley, Richard Harry.
